questions.question: Sahil Sarabhai is standing in the middle. On one side, his wife Monisha is pulling him with a force of 100 N eastward, whereas his mother, Maya is pulling him with a force of 150 N westward. What will be the net force on Sahil and towards whom will he move in the end if at all?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50N, Maya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sahil Sarabhai is experiencing two forces: 100 N eastward by Monisha and 150 N westward by Maya.
 
• The net force is calculated by subtracting the smaller force from the larger force: 150 N (westward) - 100 N (eastward) = 50 N.
 
• The direction of the net force will be towards Maya (westward), as her force is greater.
 
• Hence, the net force on Sahil is **50 N** towards **Maya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In physics, when two forces act in opposite directions, the net force is the difference between the two forces.
 
• The direction of the net force is towards the direction of the larger force.
 
• Force is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Sahil will move towards the direction where the net force is applied, which in this case is towards Maya.

questions.question: Which phylum of the animal kingdom is made up of segmented insects like earthworms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annelida** is the phylum that includes segmented worms such as earthworms.
 
• Members of the phylum **Annelida** have bodies that are divided into segments.
 
• This phylum is distinct from **Porifera** (sponges), **Nematoda** (roundworms), and **Platyhelminthes** (flatworms).
 
• Annelids exhibit a high degree of specialization in their segmented body structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **phylum Annelida** includes other organisms like leeches and polychaetes in addition to earthworms.
 
• Earthworms play a crucial role in soil health by aerating the soil and breaking down organic matter.
 
• Annelids have a coelom, which is a fluid-filled cavity that houses their internal organs and allows for greater flexibility and mobility.
 
• They have a closed circulatory system, meaning their blood is contained within vessels.
 
• The segmentation of annelids allows for more efficient and flexible movement.

questions.question: What is the term for the process of water loss from plant leaves through tiny openings called stomata?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transpiration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water is lost from plant leaves through tiny openings called stomata.
 
• Stomata are small pores found on the surface of leaves and stems that facilitate gas exchange.
 
• Transpiration helps in the movement of water and nutrients from the roots to different parts of the plant.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in maintaining the plant's temperature and facilitating photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis** is the process by which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy.
 
• **Germination** is the process by which a seed develops into a new plant.
 
• **Respiration** in plants is the process of breaking down sugar to release energy for cellular activities.
 
• Stomata are controlled by guard cells that regulate their opening and closing based on environmental conditions.
 
• Transpiration rates can be influenced by factors such as temperature, humidity, wind, and light.

questions.question: Which constitutional authority is appointed by the President of India under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution?

questions.question: Which of the following money supply measures is commonly known as the aggregate monetary resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M3** is commonly known as the aggregate monetary resources.
 
• M3 includes M1 (currency in circulation plus demand deposits) along with time deposits, providing a broader measure of the money supply.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) uses M3 to assess the overall liquidity in the economy and to formulate monetary policy.
 
• M3 is also referred to as the "broad money" measure.
 
• It reflects the total volume of money supply available in the economy at a given time, which is crucial for economic planning and analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) classifies the money supply into four categories: M1, M2, M3, and M4.
 
• M1 includes currency in circulation and demand deposits.
 
• M2 includes M1 plus savings deposits with post office savings banks.
 
• M4 includes M3 plus total post office deposits (excluding National Savings Certificates).
 
• Monitoring these measures helps in understanding the liquidity conditions and inflationary pressures in the economy.

questions.question: What is the reason behind the Indian peninsular region not showing drastic change during winters and having a moderate temperature?

• In addition to moderating temperatures, the sea also brings in moisture-laden winds, contributing to the **monsoon season**.
 
• This climatic feature is crucial for the **agriculture and overall ecology** of the region.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms belong to the Phylum Protozoa?

__

• They are characterized by their ability to move independently, often using cilia, flagella, or pseudopodia.

• The classification of organisms into different phyla is based on their unique structural and functional characteristics.
 
• Understanding the phylum of an organism helps in studying its biology, ecology, and evolutionary history.

 **CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CO₂ + H₂O + CH₃COONa**
 
• This process is an example of an acid-base reaction where the acid (vinegar) neutralizes the base (baking soda).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neutralisation reactions are important in various real-world applications, including antacid formulations to relieve indigestion and in agriculture to adjust soil pH.
 
• This reaction is also used in baking, where the carbon dioxide produced helps dough to rise.
 
• Vinegar and baking soda can also be used as a natural cleaning agent due to the abrasive action of the carbon dioxide bubbles.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common nutritional cause of anaemia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron deficiency**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron deficiency** is the most common nutritional cause of anaemia.
 
• Anaemia is a condition characterized by a lack of healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin, which are crucial for carrying oxygen to the body's tissues.
 
• Iron is a vital component of hemoglobin, and its deficiency leads to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
 
• Common symptoms of iron deficiency anaemia include fatigue, weakness, pale skin, and shortness of breath.
 
• Dietary sources of iron include red meat, poultry, fish, lentils, beans, and iron-fortified cereals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaemia** can also be caused by other factors such as vitamin B12 deficiency, folate deficiency, chronic diseases, and genetic disorders.
 
• Regular screening and blood tests can help in early detection and management of anaemia.
 
• Iron supplements and dietary modifications are common treatments for iron deficiency anaemia.
 
• In severe cases, medical interventions such as intravenous iron therapy or blood transfusions may be necessary.

questions.question: Who among the following was forced to leave his ancestral throne due to the invasion of the Uzbeks?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Babur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur**, the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in India, was forced to leave his ancestral throne in **Fergana** due to the **invasion of the Uzbeks**.
 
• The **Uzbeks**, under the leadership of **Shaibani Khan**, were a powerful force in Central Asia during Babur's time. They posed a significant threat to the region's rulers.
 
• Babur initially inherited the throne of **Fergana** (present-day Uzbekistan) at a young age. However, due to continuous invasions and internal strife, he found it difficult to maintain his rule.
 
• He faced repeated conflicts with the Uzbeks, especially under the ambitious **Shaibani Khan**, which eventually led to Babur losing his ancestral domains.
 
• After losing his kingdom, Babur wandered for a period, engaging in various battles and struggling to reclaim his territories. Eventually, he turned his focus towards India, leading to the establishment of the **Mughal Empire**.
 
• Babur's memoirs, known as the **Baburnama**, provide a detailed account of his struggles, including his conflicts with the Uzbeks and his eventual success in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shershah Suri**: A prominent ruler who established the **Sur Empire** in North India. He is known for his administrative reforms and military strategies, not for conflicts with the Uzbeks.
 
• **Genghis Khan**: The founder of the **Mongol Empire**. His era predates that of the Uzbeks' rise, and he was a conqueror rather than someone who faced displacement by the Uzbeks.
 
• **Daulat Khan Lodi**: An Afghan noble who played a role in the history of Northern India during the Mughal era. He invited Babur to India to fight against **Ibrahim Lodi**, the last Sultan of the Lodi dynasty.
 
• The historical context of **Babur** and his struggles against the Uzbeks highlights the tumultuous nature of Central Asian politics during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Understanding such events provides a deeper insight into the founding of the **Mughal Empire** and its subsequent impact on Indian history.
 
• **Mughal Empire**: Founded by Babur in 1526 after his victory over **Ibrahim Lodi** at the **First Battle of Panipat**, it became one of the largest and most influential empires in Indian history, known for its cultural and architectural achievements.

• **Bile** is the digestive juice stored in the gall bladder.
 
• The primary function of bile is to facilitate the digestion and absorption of fats in the small intestine.
 
• Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder until it is needed for digestion.
 
• It contains bile acids, which are critical for the emulsification of fats, breaking them down into smaller particles that can be more easily digested by enzymes.

• The gall bladder is a small, pear-shaped organ located beneath the liver.
 
• When food enters the small intestine, the gall bladder releases bile through the bile ducts into the small intestine to aid in digestion.
 
• **Bile acids** are derived from cholesterol and help in the digestion and absorption of dietary fats and fat-soluble vitamins.
 
• In addition to bile acids, bile also contains cholesterol, phospholipids, bilirubin, and electrolytes.

• The Indian Ocean covers approximately 20% of the Earth's water surface.
 
• It is an important route for international trade, especially for oil and petroleum products.
 
• The Indian Ocean is known for its unique marine biodiversity and significant climatic influence on the surrounding regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Ocean is the warmest ocean in the world, which affects the monsoon weather patterns in the region.
 
• It is home to several significant ports and harbors, including Mumbai, Colombo, and Durban.
 
• The ocean plays a crucial role in regulating the Earth’s climate and weather systems.
 
• It is also rich in mineral resources, including offshore oil and gas reserves.
 
• Several island nations, including the Maldives, Seychelles, and Mauritius, are located in the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Which ministry launched the KCC Ghar Ghar Abhiyaan in September 2023?

options.text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** launched the KCC Ghar Ghar Abhiyaan in September 2023.
 
• This initiative aims to promote the distribution and usage of Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) among farmers to ensure they have access to timely credit for their agricultural needs.
 
• The KCC scheme provides farmers with adequate and timely credit support from the banking system under a single window for their cultivation and other needs.
 
• The campaign is part of the government’s effort to enhance the financial inclusion of farmers and improve their economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)** scheme was introduced in 1998 to provide short-term credit to farmers.
 
• The scheme aims to meet the comprehensive credit requirements of the agriculture sector by giving farmers the flexibility to purchase agricultural inputs and draw cash for their production needs.
 
• As of recent updates, the scheme has been expanded to cover livestock, fisheries, and other allied activities, ensuring broader coverage and benefit to the rural agricultural community.
 
• The KCC Ghar Ghar Abhiyaan will include awareness campaigns, door-to-door visits, and collaboration with local banks to facilitate the issuance of KCCs.
